text:
opsbot: INCIDENT 3995556789 triggered — latency SLO breach on /v1/generate (p99 > 1.2s). Severity: P1. Auto-page to #incidents and @oncall-rotation.

mia: seeing a big jump in tail latency since 02:03 UTC, p95 ~380ms -> 540ms, p99 ~700ms -> 1.3s. Streaming stalls reported by customers (chunk gaps).

sanjay: confirmed, dashboard shows spike starts at 02:02:40. request rates steady. CPU/GPU utilization normal.

leah: logs show lots of 502s from config-fetch service upstream and retries on feature-flag resolution. suspect control-plane dependency.

bryce: adding recent traces: 
```
trace_id: 0x9f4... path: gateway -> auth -> config-fetch -> model-router -> runtime
span: config-fetch 450ms, auth 120ms, model-router 50ms
```

karen-cs: we’ve received two customer escalation emails about streaming stalls (~5–8s silent periods) and one timed-out websocket. Customers affected: acme-corp, bluewave.

oncall-rotation: I’m on it, grabbing runbook. Priorities: restore streaming tail latency, reduce p99 under 800ms, and assess customer impact.

mia: quick checklist — fallback routing to cached feature flags, disable non-critical config fetch, enable short-circuit auth cache. Can someone flip flag?

elaine-eng-sre: oncall here. I can enable auth cache bypass -> NO, sorry, enable auth cache (use token-store local TTL) for 10m. Rolling that now.

opsbot: deployment job started: enable-local-auth-cache v1.2 -> 3 hosts.

bryce: note — config-fetch backlog shows surge of retries from model-router instances, caused by a recent feature flag rollout (ff-2026-streaming-prefetch) that expanded keys.

leah: yep, rollout started 01:58 UTC. Propagation slowed due to DB paging on configstore; some config reads hit a slow secondary.

sanjay: paging on configstore DB is our bottleneck, p50 read latency 12ms -> 320ms for some keys, causing config-fetch to timeout and retry, cascading into model-router stall.

oncall-rotation: mitigation plan: 1) pause ff-2026 rollout 2) route config-fetch read traffic to primaries 3) enable short TTL local caching for feature flags 4) apply temporary rate-limit smoothing on gateway.

mia: executed step 1 (paused rollout) at 02:09:10 UTC.

elaine-eng-sre: step 2 done: updated configstore read preference to primary for the flag namespace at 02:11:00. Monitoring DB.

opsbot: routing change applied, arithmetic of affected instances: 24/24 now reading primaries.

bryce: step 3: pushing local TTL heuristic -> set flags cache TTL to 30s on runtime pool. Doing canary 5 hosts first.

leah: canary looks harmless. No regressions. Proceeding to 50% rollout.

karen-cs: customer comms: sending interim note to acme-corp and bluewave explaining we’re mitigating tail latency and will follow up once stable.

mia: gateway smoothing: add 200ms token bucket burst window to reduce short spikes of config-fetch calls. Applying now.

opsbot: rate-limit smoothing applied on gateway-edge (policy rl-smoothing-200ms).

sanjay: within 2 minutes we see p99 drop from 1.3s -> 850ms. Streaming silent gaps reduced to 1–2s.

elaine-eng-sre: DB read latency for flagged keys down to 45ms median, extremes at 180ms. Paging tapering.

mia: still seeing a few noisy model-router shards, investigating if KV cache warmup incomplete. Adding warmup at runtime for hot prefixes.

bryce: KV warmup script executed on 8 hot shards, warming common prefixes from redis-backend cache.

sanjay: after warmup p99 stabilized ~620ms, p95 ~320ms. Streaming stall reports drop to zero. Looks like control-plane read path + cache coldness were the combo.

oncall-rotation: good progress. Next steps: 1) keep feature flag rollout paused 2) follow up with data team to check secondary performance and paging root cause 3) plan a safer rollout with gradual key expansion 4) write post-incident notes and customer impact assessment.

karen-cs: I’ll gather exact list of customers affected and timestamps for CS follow-up.

leah: filing a ticket to data infra: configstore secondary paging during flag-heavy reads -> assign to @dina-data. Tag: P2 followup.

opsbot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigation in place, p99 under 800ms target, monitoring for 30m. No ongoing customer outages.

mia: anyone see any residual error spikes or retry storms?

elaine-eng-sre: small retry bursts at 02:17–02:20 but within expected after warmup. No more 502s.

sanjay: also flagging that auth token-store had ephemeral lock contention during peak, added margin in local cache to avoid future pressure.

bryce: suggest we add a preflight to flag rollouts that exercises configstore read load and simulates propagation. Will draft RFC.

karen-cs: sending customer impact note now. Will include timeline, mitigation actions, and committed follow-ups.

noncall-rotation: handing off to oncall/next shift. I’ll update the incident playbook with what we did. If any regression, page me.

opsbot: INCIDENT 3995556789 annotated: mitigated -> monitoring. Closed to P1 active response.

mia: quick retrospective items: better canary for flag key cardinality, aggressive local caching on head-of-line stalls, and consider configstore read-scaling options.

leah: logging note — increase sampling of config-fetch traces during rollouts.

sanjay: saving traces and graphs to incident folder: s3://incidents/3995556789/traces.tar.gz.

karen-cs: CS follow-up scheduled, marking impacted accounts and drafting apology + RCA timeline.

bryce: thanks all — good coordination. Closing thread unless someone wants to add action items.
